items.title: 11th HSF Kramer-NLU Delhi International Negotiation Competition: LIVE UPDATES
items.summary: National Law University (NLU) Delhi will be hosting the 11th edition of the HSF Kramer-NLU Delhi International Negotiation Competition (INC) beginning today. Organised jointly by Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer (HSF Kramer) and NLU Delhi, the competition has been held since 2014. This year's edition runs from August 21 to 23 at the University's campus in Sector-14, Dwarka. 38 teams from law schools around the world are expected to take part. Each university fields one team of two students. Participants will step into the roles of international lawyers, negotiating a series of legal problems modelled on real-life situations. Each round will be judged by a panel that includes renowned lawyers and academicians. The competition consists of two preliminary rounds followed by knock-out advanced rounds. The two advanced-round winners will then face off in the final. Today's proceedings begin at 3 PM with registration and penalty appeals of Negotiation Plans for Preliminary Rounds, followed by the inaugural ceremony, opening ceremony, and a panel discussion titled Practitioners' Masterclass on M&A. items.title: Priyank Kharge asks if RSS will sing Vande Mataram instead of Sada Vatsale
items.summary: Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge has challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah to urge the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to sing Vande Mataram in Nagpur instead of its anthem Sadaa Vatsale. Priyank Kharge, who has been at loggerheads with the RSS for several months, challenged Modi and Shah to demand that the RSS give up its anthem Sada Vatsale in favour of Vande Mataram. He made these remarks while responding to a question on whether the CJP protests were diverting attention from the Vande Mataram Bill. The Union government passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, giving Vande Mataram, the national song, the same protection as the National Anthem. This would make it a punishable offence to “intentionally prevent” the singing of the national anthem or national song, or to “cause disturbance” to an assembly engaged in such singing. Kharge said Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Rabindranath Tagore had deliberated in 1937 on which portions of the song should be sung publicly and why. “So, are they all ‘anti-national’ now?” he asked. items.title: Satyagraha and the art of dissent in Kerala: A veteran journo visits her old haunt in Tvm
items.summary: The old Secretariat Building in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram has an iconic entrance called the Satyagraha Gate. It is here that hundreds of protestors have gathered over the years. They came from different parts of the state, had different agendas, different political affiliations, and demands. On any given day, one can see protestors sitting under a makeshift canopy, holding up placards or raising slogans. During quiet breaks, they would be eating a simple meal or sleeping on a mat. If the protests are big, they can block the arterial MG (Mahatma Gandhi) Road, which stretches in front of the Secretariat. Sometimes, they can get violent too. During my years as a journalist in Thiruvananthapuram, I had interviewed a variety of satyagrahis sitting in protest at the gates. They ranged from fisherfolk and teachers, to headload workers and political dissidents. Sometimes, my car got stuck in the middle of a swelling ocean of sloganeering satyagrahis who would be amused to see the rare sight of a woman driver.
